text: Lesson 11 set an RPO of 5 minutes and an RTO of 1 hour. Lesson 23's drill either met those targets or it didn't, and rounding the results favorably afterward would defeat the entire point of running an unannounced test.

RTO is measured from when the disaster was declared to when the application was genuinely reachable again — not when the failover command ran, and not when it returned success. In this drill, that measurement came out to about 17 minutes 40 seconds, a real pass against the 1-hour target.

RPO is measured by comparing the last confirmed write on the old primary to the most recent write actually found on the new primary, using the audit log from Chapter 3. In this drill, that gap was 44 seconds, a real pass against the 5-minute target.

If either target had been missed, the correct response would be documenting exactly what happened and feeding it back into the runbook, not hiding it. Next lesson brings these real, honest results back to Overlook's leadership.
